title: CAT 2023 Question Paper (Slot 1, PYQ) - Quantitative Aptitude - Coordinate Geometry
subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.q: Let $C$ be the circle $x^2 + y^2 + 4x - 6y - 3 = 0$ and $L$ be the locus of the point of intersection of a pair of tangents to $C$ with the angle between the two tangents equal to $60^\circ$. Then, the point at which $L$ touches the line $x = 6$ is
questions.explain:
Rewrite the circle equation by completing the square: $(x+2)^2 - 4 + (y-3)^2 - 9 - 3 = 0 \implies (x+2)^2 + (y-3)^2 = 16$. This gives center $O = (-2, 3)$ and radius $r = 4$. 
The locus $L$ of the intersection of two tangents with angle $2\theta = 60^\circ$ is a concentric circle. Let $P$ be a point on $L$. In $\Delta OPQ$ (where $Q$ is the tangent point), $\sin(30^\circ) = r / OP \implies 1/2 = 4 / OP \implies OP = 8$. 
So $L$ is a circle centered at $(-2, 3)$ with radius 8: $(x+2)^2 + (y-3)^2 = 64$. 
We substitute $x = 6$ into $L$'s equation: $(6+2)^2 + (y-3)^2 = 64 \implies 64 + (y-3)^2 = 64 \implies (y-3)^2 = 0 \implies y = 3$. 
The point of intersection is $(6, 3)$.
